latest_substantive_result.summary: The producer reports a finite-temperature sufficient criterion for positional free-energy convexity in a fixed network of three-dimensional Gaussian axles: every constrained interval must contain at least one conserved nonpassing spectator, with total contour conserved on each axle and point junctions. The source also reports a finite-chain stiffness calculation and a constrained explicit-contact Monte Carlo pilot. In the pilot, split spectator placement retained a distinct residence pattern, but signed-position means were insufficiently mixed, so no equilibrium curvature or exact-flatness conclusion is made. This is a scoped model result, not a physical mechanism or practical advantage.

next_decisive_step: No follow-up work is implied by this intake. Any resumed molecular route first needs a same-interaction model or experiment establishing ring transit across the actual linker, order retention without imposed constraints, and selective A coupling with B left mobile.

limitations: The coverage condition is per constrained interval, not an average-density criterion; the source gives an empty-interval (0,2) case that can favor contraction.
No finite bulk modulus, fast sliding, uniform junction density, or robustness under topology change is established.
The explicit-contact pilot imposes piercing and ring order; signed-position means were insufficiently mixed, preventing an equilibrium-curvature or exact-flatness claim.

The alternating A/B construction still lacks demonstrated transit across actual joins, order retention without an imposed restriction, and selective coupling that preserves spectator aperture and contour transfer.
Relevant broad prior configurations are acknowledged by the source; no exact-priority or novelty review was performed by this integration.
The source calculation and contact pilot were not rerun, and no physical experiment or operation-cost measurement is included.
publication.scope: Fixed network of 3D Gaussian axles; conserved total contour on each axle; point junctions; conserved nonpassing spectator counts, with at least one spectator in every constrained interval; positional free energy after integrating over contour allocations. The source extends the condition to arbitrary spans and heterogeneous counts and to fixed convex domains for unobserved junction positions. Finite contour footprints are covered only when the remaining contour retains Gaussian statistics. The producer-reported explicit-contact pilot uses a 64-bond axle, three rigid seven-bead rings, finite-extensibility bonds, repulsive ring-axle/ring-ring interactions, confined boundaries, and imposed piercing/order constraints. It is not an equilibrium-curvature estimate, unconstrained topology test, physical experiment, or molecular rate measurement.
